title: makelattice: crystal from a unit-cell file
purpose: Exercises `makelattice` [@epsrmanual], which builds a crystal of tethered one-atom molecules by repeating a unit cell `na x nb x nc` times — the starting point for EPSR models of crystalline or amorphous network materials [@soper2005]. Three unit cells cover fractional and absolute coordinates, a cubic cell, a cell with gamma = 120° and a triclinic cell, and the optional lines of the cell file.
system: Three test crystals at 300 K. Rock salt NaCl (a = 5.64 Å, 8 atoms per cubic cell in fractional coordinates, Na: epsilon 0.5443 kJ/mol, sigma 2.35 Å, q +1; Cl: 0.4184 kJ/mol, 4.4 Å, q -1; `ecore dcore` 0.5 2.0; stored random-number state) as a 2×2×2 supercell of 64 atoms, box 11.28 Å. A triclinic Si/O cell (4.1, 4.6, 5.3 Å; 80°, 100°, 110°; absolute coordinates; 3 atoms) as 2×2×1 (12 atoms). An argon cell (3, 4, 5 Å; gamma 120°; 2 atoms) as 3×2×1 (12 atoms).
inputs: Unit-cell files written for this test: `NaCl.cell`, `tric.cell` (atom-type line without `iexchange`, no ecore line, no random-number line: generator reset) and `ortho.cell` (no coordinate-type line, count read from line 3). Commands: `makelattice NaCl.cell 2 2 2 < ml1.stdin` (output name with extension), `makelattice < ml2.stdin` (file and `na` on one line, `nb nc` prompted), `makelattice < ml3.stdin` (all prompted).
verification: Three program calls; compared outputs `NaCl_222.ato`, `tric.ato`, `ortho.ato`, all identical. The triclinic path is active: the reference `tric.ato` holds box lengths 8.2, 9.2, 5.3 Å and the converted angles 110°, 12.2387°, 145.0° from `convertalphabetagamma`.
notes: Fortran details reproduced: the box is always written as non-cubic (`cubic` is never set); `cosd`/`sind` are the gfortran intrinsics (not EPSR's own functions, since they are not declared `external`); `natomsph` is implicitly INTEGER, so `ctype` stores the bit pattern of integer 1 (1.4E-45) as `natomsphere`.
